best_for: Windows users who want to check whether an SSD or hard drive is failing before they lose data, and get warned when its health drops.
description:
CrystalDiskInfo is a drive health tool from Crystal Dew World, a software site that has been running since 1998. First released in 2008, it passed 100 million downloads in 2026. Its author says one inspiration was a 2007 Google study that linked S.M.A.R.T. data to hard drive failures.

If a drive shows yellow Caution or red Bad, the site's guide tells you what it means and what to do: back up first, to a different physical drive, then check the warranty. Caution means a watched value crossed its threshold; Bad means a value fell below the limit the maker set. The program cannot tell you the day a drive will die, but you can copy its readings as text to send to a repair shop or the manufacturer.

points.title: Reads the drive's own health data
points.text: It shows S.M.A.R.T. values, a health status and graphs for SATA, NVMe and some USB drives. NVMe support needs Windows 10 or Server 2016 or later.

points.title: Can warn you in the background
points.text: A resident mode with alarms keeps watch, and it can send alert emails when a drive's health changes. The newest email features need .NET 4.8.

points.title: RAID and some USB boxes are blind spots
points.text: It does not support most RAID disks or drives behind an add-in ATA controller, and only some USB enclosures pass the data through. If a drive does not show up, check these first.

points.title: Runs on very old Windows
points.text: It supports Windows XP through 11 and Server 2003 through 2025, on x86, x64 and Arm64. The installer itself does not run on XP or Server 2003; use the zip there.

points.title: Free and MIT licensed
points.text: The source is on GitHub under the MIT license. Besides the Standard edition there are themed editions (Shizuku, Aoi, Kurei Kei) with the same functions.

points.title: Installer or zip
points.text: Each edition comes as an installer or a zip. The installers listed here install for the whole machine, for x86, x64 and Arm64, and the Windows listing keeps 28 versions.

sources.label: What to do when CrystalDiskInfo shows Caution or Bad
